topic.title: UPI feels free because someone else pays
topic.claim: UPI feels free to us because the cost sits with the shopkeeper, and the moment it moves, you will feel it too.
topic.behaviour: We scan and pay for everything, even tiny amounts, never thinking about who covers the cost. When a fee threatens the shopkeeper, the shop starts asking for cash or a small extra.
topic.mechanism: Someone always pays for a network, whether banks, merchants or customers. A 'free' system is one where the bill is hidden from the person with the most choices.
topic.group: Everyday UPI users who pay for petrol, shopping and small bills
topic.moment: You scan the QR at the petrol pump without thinking, because paying has stopped feeling like paying.

turn.believed: UPI is free, so it costs nobody anything.
turn.actually: The cost was always there, and shops are the ones pushing back before it reaches us.

topic.feeling: a little uneasy that a habit we love has a hidden bill
topic.villain: a payment network whose costs are hidden from the people who use it most
topic.because: Banks and payment firms say they need to recover network costs. Merchants will pass any fee on to customers if they can.

proof.fact: NPCI put off a planned October 15 rollout of a 0.4% fee on eligible UPI merchant transactions above ₹2,000.

topic.payoff: After Diwali, watch the counter. The first 'cash gives a discount' board will tell you where this is going.
topic.send_to: The friend who pays for everything by UPI and never carries cash.
real_details: The fee will now start after Diwali with no new date given
Retailers and petrol pump operators opposed the fee, and some warned they could stop accepting UPI
fees on larger payments were capped at ₹300
topic.news_peg: NPCI postponed the 0.4% UPI merchant fee after retailer pushback, reported 2026-10-13
topic.why_now: The fee is only delayed until after Diwali, so the question returns within weeks.

score.why: UPI feels free because the cost sits with the shopkeeper. The first 'cash discount' board shows where this is going.
